summary: Static ArgoCD ApplicationSet FD-001 tenant metadata propagation aligns GitOps desired-state intent with backbone Helm workload labels.
claim_boundary: This slice updates source-controlled ArgoCD ApplicationSet desired-state metadata and local CI semantic smoke checks only. It does not claim ArgoCD controller reconciliation, namespace creation, sync health, cosign verification result, Kubernetes admission, OpenCost allocation/reporting, hosted CI green, branch-protection state, or production tenant workload deployment.

best_practice_research.used_for: Grounded ApplicationSet generator parameters as the list source for generated Applications.
Grounded the template metadata/spec fields that generated Applications inherit from list-generator values.
Grounded managedNamespaceMetadata plus CreateNamespace=true for desired namespace labels while avoiding a live sync claim.
Preserved common app.kubernetes.io labels alongside Oyatie tenant/cost labels.
Grounded tenant/cost labels as future allocation dimensions without claiming OpenCost output.

source_basis.use: The static ApplicationSet enumerates messenger, mail, social, and community Applications on the oyatie-cloud-provider dev track.
The ApplicationSet values mirror the FD-001 workload label defaults already present in the source Helm charts.
The static rendered Deployment snapshots provide concrete downstream workload label evidence for the same values.
The local CI smoke parses the ApplicationSet and now asserts tenant metadata semantics instead of YAML syntax only.

findings: The change extends the existing single ApplicationSet rather than adding four separate Application files.
FD-001 metadata is repeated in generator data, template labels, Helm parameters, and namespace metadata to make drift explicit and mechanically checkable.
GitOps desired state now carries the same tenant/cost/workload/regulatory dimensions as chart defaults and rendered snapshots.
The slice improves future FinOps, namespace inventory, and admission-policy inputs while preserving the no-live-sync claim boundary.
The CI smoke now rejects missing ApplicationSet tenant labels, namespace labels, Helm workload label parameters, missing chart paths, and incorrect four-service generator cardinality.
ApplicationSet annotations and evidence continue to state that this is static desired-state intent, not applied cluster state.
F3_adversarial.not_applicable_reason: This is an infrastructure metadata propagation slice, not a defect fix; adversarial coverage is the semantic smoke assertion and focused static verification.
F3_adversarial.passing_fixture_id: argocd tenant metadata static verification passed for 4 applications
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Removing any required workloadLabels.* Helm parameter or FD-001 namespace label would fail the governance smoke.

findings: Operators and future agents can see FD-001 dogfood tenant ownership directly in the ApplicationSet rather than chasing chart defaults.
ApplicationSet semantic validation covers labels, generator values, chart-path existence, Helm parameters, namespace labels, and CreateNamespace=true.
Backbone governance smoke now parses the new evidence file and asserts ApplicationSet tenant metadata.

alternatives_named: Rely only on Helm values defaults
Add four separate ArgoCD Applications with duplicated labels
Extend the existing ApplicationSet generator/template with explicit FD-001 metadata
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Extending the existing ApplicationSet keeps one GitOps source of truth, preserves the four-service list generator, and makes future sync-time overrides explicit.
rejected_reasons: Relying only on chart defaults lets GitOps promotion metadata drift silently from workload metadata.
Four separate Application files increase duplication and review surface without adding live evidence.

findings: No credentials, tokens, kubeconfigs, signing keys, or tenant records were added.
Labels are static low-cardinality classification metadata, not user data.
The ApplicationSet remains scoped to one namespace per microservice and keeps cosign-required/fail-closed annotations.
Static ApplicationSet metadata has no service request-path performance impact.
Regulatory-pack and tenant/cost labels are present for future admission, inventory, and FinOps control-plane use; no compliance enforcement is claimed.
Reverting removes ApplicationSet metadata additions, CI smoke assertions, task text, evidence, and audit rows without changing service runtime code or live infrastructure.
Application and namespace labels provide future correlation dimensions for ArgoCD inventory, Kubernetes objects, metrics, logs, traces, and cost allocation.
No ApplicationSet destination, project, sync options, chart path, or image digest placeholder semantics changed.
Label names reuse the existing oya.io and oyatie.com keys already present in Helm charts and rendered snapshots.
tasks/plan.md, tasks/todo.md, evidence, and audit-chain rows document the static desired-state scope and non-claims.
The static GitOps manifest remains under microservices/cloud-iac/iac/oyatie-cloud-provider/argocd/apps/.
The slice stays in the deployment-intent layer and does not change microservice domain/API/persistence/broker boundaries.
No Cargo, npm, Helm, ArgoCD, or provider dependency was added.
The manifest remains an argoproj.io/v1alpha1 ApplicationSet with list-generator string parameters.
Backbone CI governance smoke now asserts ApplicationSet semantics for FD-001 tenant metadata instead of parsing the YAML generically.
